events.title: .NET 3.5 and C# 3.0 with LINQ released
events.summary: Microsoft shipped .NET Framework 3.5 on November 19, 2007 with C# 3.0 LINQ, lambda expressions, and extension methods.
events.about: LINQ let C# developers query databases, XML, and in-memory collections with the same syntax: `from x in list where x.Age > 18 select x.Name`. It changed how .NET teams wrote data access — influencing Entity Framework, ORMs, and reactive patterns for a decade.

narrative.whyChosen: LINQ was the defining language feature of the C# 3 era.
narrative.whyImportant: Unified query syntax across SQL, objects, and XML was a paradigm shift for .NET.
narrative.problemSolved: C# lacked expressive, composable data queries without verbose loops or stringly-typed SQL.
